module.title: Gaussian initial conditions and Zel'dovich/2LPT perturbed fields
module.expensive_path: Real-to-complex and complex-to-real FFTW3 transforms over the DIM^3 (hi-res) and HII_DIM^3 (lo-res) grids to generate the Gaussian random field and its Zel'dovich/2LPT displacement, plus the density/velocity filtering step; this is the classic FFT-bound kernel that a GPU port (cuFFT) targets directly.
module.rationale: This is the only module proposed in the merged codebase phase (PR #508). It is the self-contained front end of the pipeline: Gaussian field generation through perturbed density/peculiar-velocity fields, stopping before halo finding and radiative transfer, which the prior module cut intentionally left for a later, separate task.
excluded: Halo catalogue and box construction (HaloBox.c, HaloCatalog.c) - downstream consumer, separate physics/task
Ionization, spin temperature and brightness temperature (IonisationBox.c, SpinTemperatureBox.c, BrightnessTemperatureBox.c) - downstream radiative physics, separate task
Interpolation tables and halo mass function machinery (interp_tables.c, hmf.c) - shared by downstream modules, not exercised by the IC/perturbation path alone
Photon conservation, luminosity function, light-cone assembly - downstream of this module's output
hazards: FFTW plan creation and OpenMP-threaded transforms are the primary source of run-to-run floating-point non-associativity; check tolerances must be derived with this in mind, not treated as bit-reproducible.
test_perturb.py's high-resolution 2LPT case is skipped upstream itself (aliasing in downsampling); no check should rely on that configuration.
